text:
elaine: Heads up — pre-merge SAST picked up a HIGH in payments-service on PR #4823. scan-bot attached output. needs triage. :eyes:

scan-bot: SAST finding RDW-SAST-2025-114; path: services/payments/src/decoder.go:42; confidence: 0.86; summary: possible insecure deserialization of external payload. evidence: `payload -> gob.NewDecoder(r)`

matt: I'll take it. Quick q: looks like our code or a vendored lib?

jamie: @matt looks like our wrapper around gob.Decoder in payments. Could be an FP but treat as real until repro. Steps: reproduce locally, add unit test, then either patch or add suppression with SEC ticket.

sanjay: @matt can you also check KMS audit logs for the payments key usage around any suspicious deployments? If we escalate to IR we need the key usage trail. tagging @ops for help.

matt: Reproduced locally — decoder used on webhook body before validation. I can craft an exploit-esque payload that causes arbitrary type decode. Drafting a patch to whitelist allowed types and fail closed. Pushing draft to PR branch now.

jamie: Good. After patch lands, schedule a DAST run against staging (post-deploy) to make sure runtime surface is covered. DAST job id we'll open in the ticket. Also add a unit test that asserts unknown type decode errors out.

elaine: Also: we need a temporary RBAC change to let the scanner-runner access the staging repo snapshot for full-path tracing. I created SEC-2213 for RBAC + auditlog request. DO NOT grant broad write perms — scanner read-only role only.

matt: Patch pushed: added strict type registry and input validation. Also added small reproducer test. PR build shows build + tests passing locally, will push to origin shortly.

jamie: Playbook update suggestion: pre-merge gating rule — any high severity SAST must have a linked SEC ticket and a triage label `sec-triaged` before CI allows merge. If suppression is used, it must include the SEC ticket and expiry date. I'll update the Confluence and CI rule.

elaine: Agreed. Example suppression format for our CI to parse:

```
// SEC-SUPPRESS: RDW-SAST-2025-114
// reason: FP - path validated by external gate
// expires: 2026-06-01
```

matt: That suppression format works for automation. Note: ensure audit logs capture who added the suppression line.

sanjay: On KMS: I'll ask infra to pull CloudKMS audit logs for key `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/payments-key` for the last 30 days and attach to SEC-2213. So far no suspicious decrypt calls correlated with this PR. Setting incident severity to P2 (investigate, no active exploit).

jamie: I'll wire the CI so that when a suppression is present it checks for `SEC-` ticket ID and that ticket must be in our security tracker with status `open` or `accepted`. If not, CI fails the gate. Also add a small audit event to record PR user + approver when suppression is merged.

elaine: Can we also make the scanner annotate the PR with a short repro snippet and a suggested remediation? That reduces back-and-forth for devs.

scan-bot: Feature request noted: annotate + suggested fixes on new SAST findings (queued).

matt: I'll update the PR description with the remediation steps and link to SEC-2213. Planning rollback if anything weird shows in staging DAST.

jamie: After patch + staging DAST, we'll close SEC-2213 with remediation notes and follow-up: add test to regression suite and add reproducible case to our eval harness.

elaine: Thanks team. Action items: 1) @matt push fix & tests (in progress) 2) @sanjay pull KMS audit logs and attach to SEC-2213 3) @jamie update CI/playbook for suppression parsing + triage label 4) me — update Confluence and notify ops for RBAC change in staging.

matt: on it.

sanjay: pulling logs now, will post link in the ticket when done.

elaine: :thumbsup:
